answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may endorse a task, then slash that stake if independent audits find fabricated work. A prism of reviewers samples claims, while an echo of repeated endorsements from the same funding source counts as one signal, not many. This raises the attacker’s cost: creating sybils ties up real capital, and detected fraud burns it, so scaling fake identities toward the zenith becomes costly rather than free.
